cases.sentence: Графиня, у которой разболелась голова от суеты и шума, лежала в новой диванной с ___ на голове.
cases.explain: «уксусными повязками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The voices and footsteps of the many servants and of the peasants who had come with the carts resounded as they shouted to one another in the yard and in the house. The count had been out since morning. The countess had a headache brought on by all the noise and turmoil and was lying down in the new sitting room with a vinegar compress on her head. Pétya was not at home, he had gone to visit a friend with whom he meant to obtain a transfer from the militia to the active army. Sónya was in the ballroom looking after the packing of the glass and china. Natásha was sitting on the floor of her dismantled room with dresses, ribbons, and scarves strewn all about her, gazing fixedly at the floor and holding in her hands the old ball dress (already out of fashion) which she had worn at her first Petersburg ball.

cases.sentence: Наташа, накинув белый ___ на волосы и придерживая его обеими руками за кончики, вышла на улицу.
cases.explain: «носовой платок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Natásha, throwing a clean pocket handkerchief over her hair and holding an end of it in each hand, went out into the street.

cases.sentence: ___, старушка Мавра Кузьминишна, отделилась от толпы, стоявшей у ворот и, подойдя к телеге, на которой была рогожная кибиточка, разговаривала с лежавшим в этой телеге молодым, бледным офицером.
cases.explain: «Бывшая ключница» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The former housekeeper, old Mávra Kuzmínichna, had stepped out of the crowd by the gate, gone up to a cart with a hood constructed of bast mats, and was speaking to a pale young officer who lay inside. Natásha moved a few steps forward and stopped shyly, still holding her handkerchief, and listened to what the housekeeper was saying.

cases.sentence: — Не знаю, позволят ли, — ___ сказал офицер.
cases.explain: «слабым голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I don’t know if it would be allowed,” replied the officer in a weak voice. “Here is our commanding officer … ask him,” and he pointed to a stout major who was walking back along the street past the row of carts.

cases.sentence: Наташа испуганными глазами заглянула в лицо ___ и тотчас же пошла навстречу майору.
cases.explain: «раненого офицера» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Natásha glanced with frightened eyes at the face of the wounded officer and at once went to meet the major.

cases.sentence: Наташа слегка наклонила голову и ___ вернулась к Мавре Кузьминишне, стоявшей над офицером и с жалобным участием разговаривавшей с ним.
cases.explain: «быстрыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: With a slight inclination of her head, Natásha stepped back quickly to Mávra Kuzmínichna, who stood talking compassionately to the officer.

cases.sentence: Наташа слегка наклонила голову и быстрыми шагами вернулась к Мавре Кузьминишне, стоявшей над офицером и с ___ разговаривавшей с ним.
cases.explain: «жалобным участием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: With a slight inclination of her head, Natásha stepped back quickly to Mávra Kuzmínichna, who stood talking compassionately to the officer.

cases.sentence: Офицер в кибиточке завернул во двор Ростовых, и десятки телег с ранеными стали, по приглашениям ___, заворачивать в дворы и подъезжать к подъездам домов Поварской улицы.
cases.explain: «городских жителей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The cart in which the officer lay was turned into the Rostóvs’ yard, and dozens of carts with wounded men began at the invitation of the townsfolk to turn into the yards and to draw up at the entrances of the houses in Povarskáya Street. Natásha was evidently pleased to be dealing with new people outside the ordinary routine of her life. She and Mávra Kuzmínichna tried to get as many of the wounded as possible into their yard.

cases.sentence: Офицер в кибиточке завернул во двор Ростовых, и десятки телег с ранеными стали, по приглашениям городских жителей, заворачивать в дворы и подъезжать к подъездам домов ___.
cases.explain: «Поварской улицы» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The cart in which the officer lay was turned into the Rostóvs’ yard, and dozens of carts with wounded men began at the invitation of the townsfolk to turn into the yards and to draw up at the entrances of the houses in Povarskáya Street. Natásha was evidently pleased to be dealing with new people outside the ordinary routine of her life. She and Mávra Kuzmínichna tried to get as many of the wounded as possible into their yard.

cases.sentence: Наташе, видимо, понравились эти, вне ___ жизни, отношения с новыми людьми.
cases.explain: «обычных условий» — after the preposition «вне», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The cart in which the officer lay was turned into the Rostóvs’ yard, and dozens of carts with wounded men began at the invitation of the townsfolk to turn into the yards and to draw up at the entrances of the houses in Povarskáya Street. Natásha was evidently pleased to be dealing with new people outside the ordinary routine of her life. She and Mávra Kuzmínichna tried to get as many of the wounded as possible into their yard.

cases.sentence: Наташе, видимо, понравились эти, вне обычных условий жизни, отношения с ___.
cases.explain: «новыми людьми» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The cart in which the officer lay was turned into the Rostóvs’ yard, and dozens of carts with wounded men began at the invitation of the townsfolk to turn into the yards and to draw up at the entrances of the houses in Povarskáya Street. Natásha was evidently pleased to be dealing with new people outside the ordinary routine of her life. She and Mávra Kuzmínichna tried to get as many of the wounded as possible into their yard.

cases.sentence: Наташа побежала в дом и на цыпочках вошла в полуотворенную дверь диванной, из которой пахло уксусом и ___.
cases.explain: «гофманскими каплями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Natásha ran into the house and went on tiptoe through the half-open door into the sitting room, where there was a smell of vinegar and Hoffman’s drops.

cases.sentence: Графиня с ___ посматривала на веселое, разгоряченное лицо своего сына в то время, как он говорил это.
cases.explain: «робким ужасом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The countess looked with timid horror at her son’s eager, excited face as he said this. She realized that if she said a word about his not going to the battle (she knew he enjoyed the thought of the impending engagement) he would say something about men, honor, and the fatherland—something senseless, masculine, and obstinate which there would be no contradicting, and her plans would be spoiled; and so, hoping to arrange to leave before then and take Pétya with her as their protector and defender, she did not answer him, but after dinner called the count aside and implored him with tears to take her away quickly, that very night if possible. With a woman’s involuntary loving cunning she, who till then had not shown any alarm, said that she would die of fright if they did not leave that very night. Without any pretense she was now afraid of everything.
